claims.text: A hybrid high-throughput CALPHAD and machine-learning framework can accurately predict melting temperatures and entropies of fusion for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Standard DFT struggles with refractory HEAs because of configurational entropy and lattice distortion in disordered multicomponent systems.
NbMoTaW and HfMoTaTiZr are examples of disordered equiatomic or near-equiatomic refractory HEAs in solid-solution states with high configurational entropy.
High-throughput CALPHAD can screen thousands of compositions for phase stability and approximate melting temperatures.
Machine learning based on Holder means of elemental properties and structural data can refine predictions of entropy of fusion and heat capacity.
The machine-learning model can be specifically calibrated for disordered BCC and FCC lattices.
Configurational entropy and lattice distortion stabilize the solid-solution phase and influence the thermodynamic gap between solid and liquid states.
Holder-mean descriptors and CALPHAD thermodynamic databases capture configurational-entropy and lattice-distortion effects.
DFT has a high computational cost for sampling the configurational space of disordered HEAs.
DFT has difficulty modeling entropy of fusion accurately in disordered HEAs.
A CALPHAD-based high-throughput method efficiently screened 3246 Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti compositions and identified candidates satisfying melting-temperature and phase-fraction criteria.
Holder-mean machine-learning models predicted shear and bulk moduli of BCC NbTaTiV with relative errors of 2.5% and 6%, respectively.
Success of Holder-mean descriptors for elastic moduli supports extrapolating the model to melting properties.
CALPHAD supplies a thermodynamic baseline for phase transitions in the proposed hybrid model.
The hybrid method will predict refractory-HEA melting temperatures within 5% error and entropy of fusion within 10% error.
DFT showed deviations greater than 15% for Young's and shear moduli in the NbTaTiV comparison.
The hybrid workflow can identify alloys with melting temperatures above 1250 °C and specified phase fractions.
The method is valid only where reliable binary and ternary thermodynamic database descriptions exist.
The method may fail for immiscibility gaps caused by extreme positive mixing enthalpies, including the stated Cr-rich Fe/Co/Ni interactions.
Training a model on ordered compounds may reduce its accuracy for disordered alloys because of lattice-distortion effects, and CALPHAD accuracy depends on database quality.

contradictions.description: The claimed performance is within 5% for melting temperature and 10% for entropy of fusion, but the hypothesis is falsified only above 10% and 15%, respectively. Results outside the claimed accuracy could therefore still pass the stated falsification rule.

The boundary requires reliable thermodynamic database coverage, whereas the proposed experiment selects a composition described as not included in the CALPHAD database, potentially testing the method outside its declared domain.
